gloss: be fruitful, bear fruit; fruit, offspring
summary: The verb is to bear fruit: of a plant putting out its fruit, and of living things, people above all, increasing in number, as God commands at creation and after the flood, “be fruitful and multiply” (Gen 1:28; 9:1), and as he promises Abraham and Jacob, “I will make you fruitful” (Gen 17:6; 48:4). The noun פְּרִי is what is borne: the fruit of a tree, the produce of the ground, the “fruit of the womb”, children (Gen 30:2; Psa 127:3), and the fruit of a man's ways, what his deeds bring back on him (Jer 17:10). Phoenician pr, Ugaritic pr and Ge'ez fəre “fruit” and faraya “bear fruit” are the same root. Joseph named his son Ephraim because “God has made me fruitful” (Gen 41:52).

words.summary: What a tree, the ground or a body brings forth: fruit, crops, children. From these it is used of what a person's ways, words and deeds bring forth, which he will eat (Isa 3:10; Pro 18:21).

senses.definition: The fruit a tree or vine bears, with its seed in it, eaten as food.

evidence.note: “A עֵץ פְּרִי making פְּרִי after its kind, whose seed is in it”: the fruit carries the seed of its own kind.
“Every tree in which is the פְרִי of a tree yielding seed: to you it shall be for food.”
The woman “took of its פְּרִי and ate”; also Gen 3:2–3.
Fruit trees planted in the land: their פְּרִי is uncircumcised three years, holy in the fourth (Lev 19:24–25).
At סֻכּוֹת, on the first day, “you shall take for yourselves פְּרִי עֵץ הָדָר”, fruit of a goodly tree, with palm fronds and branches, and rejoice before Yahweh seven days.
“The land shall give its יְבוּל and the tree of the field shall give its פְּרִי”; withheld in Lev 26:20.
The spies are to bring “of the פְּרִי of the land”; they return with it (Num 13:26–27).
The man whose delight is in the law is “like a tree planted by streams of water that gives its פְּרִי in its season”.
The man who trusts in Yahweh is a tree by the water that “does not cease from making פֶּרִי”.
“He who tends a fig tree will eat its פְּרִי.”
“Like an apple tree among the trees of the forest … his פְּרִי is sweet to my taste.”
By the river from the sanctuary every tree for food: “its leaf shall not wither and its פְּרִי shall not fail; it shall bear new fruit every month … its פְּרִי for food and its leaf for healing.”
“עֵץ פְּרִי and all cedars” praise Yahweh.

senses.definition: What the ground yields at harvest: grain and the fruit of vine and tree together, brought as firstfruits and tithe.

evidence.note: “Cain brought of the פְּרִי of the ground an offering to Yahweh.”
“You shall take of the first of all the פְּרִי of the ground” in a basket to the place Yahweh chooses.
The tithe of the land, “of the seed of the land, of the פְּרִי of the tree”, is holy to Yahweh.
“Blessed the fruit of your womb and the פְּרִי of your ground and the fruit of your cattle.”
Under the curse the locust takes possession of the trees and “the פְּרִי of your ground”.
They sow fields and plant vineyards, “and make פְּרִי of harvest”.
“A land of פְּרִי into a salt waste, for the evil of those who dwell in it.”
“In that day the branch of Yahweh shall be beauty and glory, and the פְּרִי of the land pride and splendour for the escaped of Israel.”
“I will multiply the פְּרִי of the tree and the increase of the field”, so that Israel bears no more the reproach of famine among the nations.
Israel restored: “they shall make gardens and eat their פְּרִי”.
“They shall plant vineyards and eat their פְּרִי.”
The firstfruits “of all פְּרִי of every tree, year by year, to the house of Yahweh”.

senses.definition: Children, the young of the body; mostly in פְּרִי בֶטֶן, “fruit of the womb”, and of cattle as well as people.

evidence.note: Jacob to Rachel: “Am I in the place of God, who has withheld from you פְּרִי־בָטֶן?”
“Sons are a heritage from Yahweh, פְּרִי הַבָּטֶן a reward”: the parallel sets the fruit of the womb beside sons.
“Shall I give my firstborn for my transgression, פְּרִי בִטְנִי for the sin of my soul?”
“You shall eat פְרִי־בִטְנְךָ, the flesh of your sons and your daughters”, in the siege.
Yahweh swore to David: “מִפְּרִי בִטְנְךָ I will set on your throne”; Peter applies it to Christ (Act 2:30).
“He will bless the fruit of your womb and the fruit of your ground.”
Fruit of the womb and “fruit of your cattle”, the young of the herd.
“They will have no pity on פְרִי־בֶטֶן; their eye will not spare sons.”
“Shall women eat their פְּרִי, the children they have cared for?”
“Ephraim is struck, their root dried up, they shall make no פְּרִי; even if they bear, I will kill the beloved of their womb.”
“Their פְּרִי you will destroy from the earth, and their seed from among the sons of man.”
From the serpent's root comes an adder, “and its פְּרִי a flying fiery serpent”.

senses.gloss: fruit of one's ways, outcome, reward
senses.definition: What a man's deeds, thoughts, words or labour bring forth and bring back on him: he eats the fruit of his ways, for good or ill.

evidence.note: “I Yahweh search the heart … to give to each man according to his ways, according to the פְּרִי of his deeds.”
“Say of the righteous that it is well, for they shall eat the פְרִי of their deeds”; the wicked are repaid by the work of his hands (Isa 3:11).
“They shall eat of the פְּרִי of their way and be filled with their own counsels.”
“I bring evil on this people, the פְּרִי of their thoughts.”
“I will punish you according to the פְּרִי of your deeds.”
The land desolate “because of the פְּרִי of their deeds”.
“You have ploughed wickedness, reaped iniquity, eaten the פְּרִי of lies.”
Yahweh will punish “the פְּרִי of the greatness of heart of the king of Assyria”.
“From the פְּרִי of a man's mouth he is filled with good.” Also Pro 13:2; 18:20.
“Death and life are in the power of the tongue, and those who love it will eat its פְּרִי.”
“Give her of the פְּרִי of her hands.”
“The פְּרִי of the righteous is a tree of life.”
“You have turned justice into poison and the פְּרִי of righteousness into wormwood.”
“Surely there is פְּרִי for the righteous; surely there is a God who judges in the earth”: reward.
Wisdom: “My פְּרִי is better than gold, and my increase than choice silver.”
“This is all the פְּרִי of taking away his sin”: the altars broken and the Asherim gone.

evidence.locator: Gen.1.11, פְּרִי → καρπόν; Gen.30.2, Lev.23.40, Psa.132.11, Pro.11.30, Hos.14.9 the same; καρπός renders פְּרִי ×78

evidence.note: David knew “that God had sworn with an oath to him that ἐκ καρποῦ of his loins … he would raise up the Christ to sit on his throne”: Psa 132:11's פְּרִי בִטְנְךָ.
“Blessed is ὁ καρπός of your womb”: פְּרִי בֶטֶן.
“By their καρπῶν you will know them”: the good tree makes good fruit and the bad bad (Mat 7:17–20; 12:33), the fruit of one's deeds.
“Make καρπὸν worthy of repentance.”
“The καρπός of the Spirit is love, joy, peace …”
The tree of life by the river “yielding its καρπόν every month”, its leaves for healing: Ezk 47:12.

parallels.note: The yield of the land, beside the tree's fruit.
Root below and fruit above: the whole tree, and so the whole life of a people.

evidence.note: “I destroyed his פְּרִי from above and his roots from beneath.”
The remnant of Judah “shall take root downward and make פְרִי upward”; also 2Ki 19:30.

words.gloss: bear fruit, be fruitful; make fruitful
words.summary: Qal, bear fruit: of a branch or vine, and of living things and people increasing in number, nearly always beside רָבָה “multiply”. Hiphil, make fruitful: always God's doing, in his promises to Abraham, Ishmael and Jacob and the covenant of Lev 26:9, and in Joseph's naming of Ephraim.

senses.definition: Of living creatures and people: bring forth young and so grow in number, filling the earth or the land.

evidence.note: God blessed the creatures of sea and air: “פְּרוּ and multiply and fill the waters in the seas.”
To the man and woman: “פְּרוּ and multiply and fill the earth and subdue it.”
The creatures leave the ark “that they may swarm on the earth and be fruitful and multiply on the earth”.
To Noah and his sons, the blessing renewed: “פְּרוּ and multiply and fill the earth.” Again Gen 9:7.
To Jacob: “I am אֵל שַׁדַּי; פְּרֵה and multiply; a nation and an assembly of nations shall come from you.”
Isaac at Rehoboth: “Yahweh has made room for us, וּפָרִינוּ in the land.”
Israel in Goshen “were fruitful and multiplied greatly”.
“The sons of Israel פָּרוּ and swarmed and multiplied and grew exceedingly strong, and the land was filled with them.”
Yahweh will drive out the nations little by little “until you are fruitful and inherit the land”.
The remnant gathered from all lands to its fold: “they shall be fruitful and multiply.”
“When you multiply and are fruitful in the land in those days”, the ark of the covenant will no more be remembered.
“I will multiply on you man and beast, and they shall multiply and be fruitful.”

senses.gloss: bear fruit (of a plant); bring forth
senses.definition: Of a branch, bough or vine: carry fruit. The participle פֹּרִיָּה, פֹּרָת is “fruitful”. Figuratively, of what a root or the earth brings forth.

evidence.note: “A shoot shall come out of the stump of Jesse, and a branch from his roots יִפְרֶה.”
Gleanings left as when an olive tree is beaten: “four, five on its branches, פֹּרִיָּה.”
“Your mother was like a vine planted by the waters; פֹּרִיָּה and full of branches.”
“Your wife like a גֶפֶן פֹּרִיָּה within your house, your sons like olive shoots.”
Mourning “for the fruitful vine”.
“Joseph is בֵּן פֹּרָת, a fruitful one, a fruitful one by a spring.”
Anyone turning from Yahweh to the nations' gods is “a root פֹּרֶה poison and wormwood”: bearing it as fruit.
“Let the earth open, וְיִפְרוּ salvation, and let righteousness spring up together.”

senses.definition: Make a man or a people grow in number. God is always the subject, and the word belongs to his promise to the fathers.

evidence.note: To Abraham: “וְהִפְרֵתִי you exceedingly, and I will make you nations, and kings shall come from you.”
Of Ishmael: “I will bless him and make him fruitful and multiply him exceedingly.”
Isaac's blessing on Jacob: “May אֵל שַׁדַּי bless you and make you fruitful and multiply you.”
Jacob recalls God's word at Luz: “Behold, מַפְרְךָ and I will multiply you … and give this land to your seed after you.”
Joseph names his second son אֶפְרָיִם, “for God הִפְרַנִי in the land of my affliction.”
“I will turn to you and make you fruitful and multiply you, and I will establish my covenant with you.”
“He made his people very fruitful and made them stronger than their adversaries”: Exo 1:7.

senses.definition: Of Ephraim, with no object: flourish, bear fruit. Spelled יַפְרִיא, with א.

evidence.note: Of Ephraim (Hos 13:12): “Though he יַפְרִיא among his brothers, an east wind shall come, the wind of Yahweh”: a play on the name.

evidence.locator: Gen.1.28, פְּרוּ → αὐξάνεσθε; Gen.48.4, Lev.26.9, Psa.105.24, Jer.23.3 the same verb; Exo.1.7 ηὐξήθησαν; αὐξάνω renders פָּרָה ×15

evidence.note: Stephen: “As the time of the promise drew near which God had sworn to Abraham, the people ηὔξησεν and multiplied in Egypt”: Exo 1:7 told as the promise of Gen 17:6 coming true.
“Bearing fruit in every good work and αὐξανόμενοι in the knowledge of God”: the pair of Gen 1:28 turned to the believer's life; also Col 1:6.

parallels.note: “Swarm”, of creatures and of Israel in Egypt.

words.gloss: precinct, colonnade (on the west of the temple)
words.summary: A structure or open court on the west side of the temple, spelled פַּרְוָר in Kings and פַּרְבָּר in Chronicles. Its link to the root's sense of fruit is not understood: the doubled ר and the ו/ב alternation look like a foreign word, and no cognate has been found for it, so its place under this root rests only on its letters.

senses.definition: A place on the west side of the house of Yahweh, beside the chambers, with a road leading to it: a court or colonnade.

evidence.note: Josiah removed the horses given to the sun “from the entrance of the house of Yahweh, by the chamber of Nathan-melech the officer, which was בַּפַּרְוָרִים”.
The gatekeepers: “לַפַּרְבָּר westward, four at the highway and two לַפַּרְבָּר.”

words.summary: The Peshitta's ܦܐܪܐ (pēʾrā), its word for καρπός throughout the New Testament, with the same three uses as Hebrew פְּרִי: the fruit of a tree, the fruit of the womb, and the fruit of a life. The א is a spelling of Syriac's own; the word is פְּרִי.

senses.definition: What a tree or vine bears.

evidence.note: Peshitta: every good tree makes good פארא, and the bad tree bad פארא.
Peshitta: “I am the vine and you the branches; he who abides in me … bears much פארא.”
Peshitta: the tree of life “makes twelve פארא, and every month gives its fruits”: Ezk 47:12.
Peshitta: “blessed is the פארא of your womb (דבכרסכי)”.
Peshitta: “from the פארא of your belly (דכרסכ)” he would seat one on your throne: the Hebrew of Psa 132:11, מִפְּרִי בִטְנְךָ, word for word.

senses.definition: What a man's repentance, righteousness, praise or the Spirit in him brings forth.

evidence.note: Peshitta: “by their פארא you shall know them.”
Peshitta: “make פארא that is worthy of repentance.”
Peshitta: “the פארא of the Spirit is love, joy, peace …”
Peshitta: the sacrifice of praise, “the פארא of the lips that confess his name”.
Peshitta: “the פארא of righteousness is sown in peace.”

cognates.gloss: fruit; the fruit of one's labour, wealth
cognates.note: Eshmunazor of Sidon curses whoever opens his tomb: “may they have no root below nor fruit above”, the pairing of Amo 2:9 and Isa 37:31.

evidence.note: “n.m. 1. FRUIT … 2. FRUIT(S) of one's labor, WEALTH”; RES 1925 mlqṭ prt “the fruit-picker”; KAI 14.11/12 šrš lmṭ wpr lmʿl.

evidence.locator: SEM001036 pry [fruit] N: PUN001690 pr [fruit] N

cognates.note: Set beside Ge'ez fəre as an example of Ugaritic p for Ethiopic f; from the scan's OCR, not yet checked against a Ugaritic text.

evidence.locator: p. 24, Ugaritic p = Ethiopic f: pr, fre “fruit”
evidence.note: OCR read only.
“Com. Eth. ፍሬ fre (Tna. firē) ‘fruit, seed, issue’ … Tna. ፈረየ vb. ‘bear fruit, produce’, of a root fry” (OCR read only).

cognates.gloss: fruit; produce of the earth; offspring of the womb; fruit of one's deeds
cognates.note: Its uses run exactly as פְּרִי's: fruit of trees, the earth's produce, “fruit of the womb”, and the fruit of labour and of deeds.

evidence.note: “1) flos, surculus, germen … 2) fructus, plantarum, arborum … a) terrae fructus, fruges, proventus … b) uteri, i. e. soboles, proles, fetus … c) trsl.: fructus laboris, facinoris”.
ፍሬ “fruit, seed, issue” (OCR read only).

cognates.gloss: blossom; bear fruit; be fertile (of a woman); causative, make fruitful
cognates.note: Both the qal's uses are here, of plants and of a woman; the causative “make fruitful” answers to the hiphil.

evidence.note: “1) gemmas et flores emittere, florescere … 3) fructum ferre, fructificare, proprie de plantis … c) fecundam fieri, de muliere”; II,1 “facere ut floreat vel fructum ferat … fecundum reddere”.

evidence.locator: SEM000713 pry [fruit] V: GEZ001771 farya [bear] V

evidence.note: “= h. פֶּרִי, fruit, crop”, citing B. Bath. 36ᵇ פ׳ רבא “the large crop (of grain)”; transferred, usufruct.
“to increase, grow. B. Bath. 18ᵇ הדר פָּארֵי it will grow again.”

cognates.note: Its sense of shoot and offspring fits the root, but its third letter is ʾ, not y; it may belong rather with Hebrew פֹּארָה “bough” (root פאר). Hos 13:15 spells the hiphil יַפְרִיא, with א.

evidence.locator: armep x000014730, perʾu [bud] N (meanings: bud, descendant, leaf, offspring, shoot, young animal)

cognates.note: Set with Ge'ez faraya under one root “bear fruit” in Anderson–Moser's sets; the third letter is ʾ, as with perʾu.

doctrine.statement: On the third day God made the tree “making fruit after its kind, whose seed is in it” (Gen 1:11–12): each fruit carries the seed of its own kind and brings forth that kind again. On the fifth and sixth days he blessed the creatures of sea and air and then the man and woman with the same word, “be fruitful and multiply and fill” (Gen 1:22, 28), and gave them the fruit of the trees for food (Gen 1:29). After the flood the blessing is spoken again to Noah and his sons, from whom the whole earth is filled (Gen 8:17; 9:1, 7). Fruitfulness is God's blessing laid on what he made, and it works within the kinds as he made them.

The hiphil, “I will make you fruitful”, is God's promise to Abraham, joined to kings coming from him and to the land given to his seed (Gen 17:6; 48:4), and is passed to Isaac's son Jacob (Gen 28:3; 35:11) and set in the covenant (Lev 26:9). Scripture records it kept: Israel “were fruitful and multiplied greatly” in Egypt (Gen 47:27; Exo 1:7; Psa 105:24), and Stephen says this happened “as the time of the promise drew near which God had sworn to Abraham” (Act 7:17). Joseph's naming of Ephraim owns the same hand: “God has made me fruitful in the land of my affliction” (Gen 41:52). The prophets carry the promise to the regathering: the remnant brought back from all lands shall be fruitful and multiply in the land (Jer 23:3; Ezk 36:11).

Yahweh swore to David, “of the fruit of your body (מִפְּרִי בִטְנְךָ) I will set on your throne” (Psa 132:11). Peter says David knew God had sworn this of the Christ, whom he raised from the dead to sit on David's throne (Act 2:30–31), and Elizabeth calls Jesus “the fruit of your womb” to Mary (Luk 1:42). Isaiah's branch from the roots of Jesse “bears fruit” (Isa 11:1). Christ is, then, David's own offspring, born of Mary's body, and the throne he is to sit on is David's.

Yahweh searches the heart “to give to each man according to his ways, according to the fruit of his deeds” (Jer 17:10; 32:19): the righteous “eat the fruit of their deeds” (Isa 3:10) and the wicked “the fruit of their way” (Pro 1:31) and “the fruit of lies” (Hos 10:13). The New Testament takes up the same figure: a tree is known by its fruit (Mat 7:16–20; 12:33), and men are told to bring forth fruit worthy of repentance (Mat 3:8). What a life brings forth is what it will be judged by.

The curse of the law takes the land's fruit (Lev 26:20; Deu 28:42), and the prophets promise it back when Israel is restored: the mountains of Israel will bear their fruit for Yahweh's people (Ezk 36:8), the fruit of the tree will be multiplied so that they suffer famine's reproach among the nations no more (Ezk 36:30), and they shall plant vineyards and eat their fruit (Amo 9:14; Isa 65:21). From the house of Yahweh a river runs with trees on its banks whose fruit does not fail and whose leaf is for healing (Ezk 47:12), which John sees again as the tree of life (Rev 22:2). The promise is of the land of Israel made fruitful again under God's rule on the earth.

note: Left out: פֶּרֶז (BDB q.cv.ai, Hab 3:14 פְּרָזָיו, no tokens filed under the key) is spelled with ז and belongs with פְּרָזוֹן (Jdg 5:7, 11) under פרז; the place פַּרְוַיִם (q.cv.ag, 2Ch 3:6 “gold of Parvaim”) is a place name; the man פֻּרָה, Gideon's servant (q.cv.af, Jdg 7:10–11), is a name for its own entry (not written here), though its tie to this root is uncertain (it may be פֹּארָה “bough”, root פאר). פָּרָה “cow” and פַּר “bull” are another root (פרר, q.dn.ab, q.dn.ac). The cross-reference keys q.cs.ae (פֵּרְבָּר), q.da.ac and q.ds.ai (פֹּרָת) carry no tokens and are not claimed. Abbott-Smith/Thayer set καρπός beside פְּרִי, but καρπός is Greek's own word (Latin carpo), not a loan, so it is kept only as the Septuagint's rendering. MACULA lemmatises Hos 13:15 יַפְרִיא under פָּרָא; the database files it under this verb's hiphil, and the play on Ephraim (Hos 13:12) supports that. Leads not followed: Egyptian prt “fruit; seed; posterity” (TLA tla60310) and prj “come forth” are Egyptian's own words and not loans into Hebrew, so not recorded; Sabaean WFR II “produce crops (?)” (Biella p. 155), which Biella herself compares with Hebrew פָּרָה only as perhaps, has a different root and is not recorded; Arabic shows no cognate (Lane's فري is “slit”, فرو “fur”). Ugaritic pr rests on Fisher's OCR; check it in a Ugaritic dictionary or text. Persian farwār has been proposed for פַּרְוָר; no Persian dictionary is in sources.json.
